correctness.rationale: With 2<=m<=n, f:V(K_m box K_n)->{0,1,2,3,4} satisfies f(v)+sum_{u neighbor, f(u)>0}(f(u)-1)>=3 for f(v)<3, using open neighborhoods. Writing a_ij=max(f_ij-1,0), row r_i and column c_j surplus, B=sum r_i=sum c_j and T=#positive cells gives exact weight W=B+T. At labels 0,1,2 the necessary and sufficient row-column inequalities are r_i+c_j>=3, >=2, >=3, respectively (label 2 self surplus counted twice). If some column has c_j=0, every row incurs weight >=4, so W>=4m. Otherwise T>=n: if all rows r_i>=2 then W>=2m+n; if a row r_i=0 then every c_j>=2 and W>=3n; if some row r_i=1, writing a=#columns of surplus one, each such column needs two positive cells, so T>=n+a and B>=2n-a, hence W>=3n. The two explicit construction schemes yield 4m when n>=2m and 2m+n when m<=n<=2m. I independently enumerated all sub-bound assignments for six small boards (122,882,6075,49296,22330,272090 cases) with no counterexample; all-order proof is the surplus argument and the explicit construction, not these finite searches.
